main_text.l: OS magnum, quod magna Dei miracula
narrat, Quae nostros tantum cernere fecit

l.i: avos, Dum vox imbellis populi & suspiria mixta
Sanguine ruperunt vincula dura Erebi, Regnaque quaßarunt, & celso culmine
structum Mundique æquatum finibus imperium, Pondere sub cuius, nutantis vulnere vasto,
Iam pridem rerum machina tota gemit:
Dum tener astuti rejecit frena PHILIPPI Belga vovens soli libera corda Deo.
Qualia non Tacitus non aurea vena Maronis Explicuit sive bis doctius ingenium.
Os felix, cui tanta datum est nudare nepoti
Risuro fumos labilis imperij, WINSEMII; quod nec voluit
mors dura silère. Verba etenim seclis pagina tradet anus:

main_text.l: Honori Collegae dum vivebat amandi & observandi, post obitum desiderati, raptim ponebat.
Theol. & Ling. Hebraea Professor, ac pro tempore Rector in Acad. Franekerana.

page.notes: The initial O is a large woodcut letter. Several lines of the verse are set in italic; the first letter of the poem is the woodcut initial. The word "In" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment starting the next section. Some words are doubtful due to scan quality, notably "Qualia" and "Risuro", which are transcribed as printed.
